study_identification.title: Characterizing the distinct imaging phenotypes, clinical behavior, and genetic vulnerability of brain maturational subtypes in mood disorders

study_characteristics.study_objective: To quantify brain morphological heterogeneity in mood disorders by mapping region-level gray matter volume changes at individual patient level, using normative modeling and unsupervised clustering to identify subtypes in patients with MDD and BD, then characterize resulting subtypes using clinical behaviors, cell-specific transcriptomic profiles, and polygenic risk scores.

dataset_name.answer: Discovery cohort: First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University (Shenyang, China); Validation cohort: First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University (Shenyang, China)

hc_age.answer: mean 29.0; sd 9.3; min NR; max NR

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12 (Computation Anatomy Toolbox); SPM12 (Statistical Parametric Mapping); VBM (voxel-based morphometry); Desikan-Killiany (DK) parcellation atlas (68 cortical regions)

quality_checking_detail.answer: Automated weighted average image quality rating (IQR) included in CAT12 toolbox. Cut-off applied: IQR >=80%, grade >= B to ensure high quality images. Images classified as failed QC if noise grade <= C (70%) and total IQR grade < B (80%). General IQR ratings in discovery cohort: 86.4% ± 0.74% (mean ± sd) in Dataset 1 and 86.3% ± 0.72% (mean ± sd) in Dataset 2.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Single-site study conducted at the First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China using a Signa HDx 3.0T MRI system (GE Healthcare).

software_tool.answer: Not explicitly specified; custom implementation in the context described

response_variable.answer: Regional gray matter volume (GMV) density for 68 cortical regions (Desikan-Killiany parcellation)

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex used to create normative range. Specific fixed/random effect modeling not explicitly described for the quantile regression normative model.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper does not describe explicit evaluation of how well the normative model handles nuisance structure such as heteroscedasticity, non-linearity, or correlation structure. The quantile regression method is described for estimating 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles as a function of age and sex, but no validation metrics (e.g., explained variance, MSLL, skewness, kurtosis of z-scores) are reported to confirm the model appropriately captures the data's nuisance structure.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Quantile regression was used to obtain a normative range of regional GMV variation as a function of age and sex descripted in a previous study (Lv et al., 2021). We positioned individuals with MDD and BD on the normative percentile charts based on HC and expressed three kinds of continuous measurement of deviation from the generated normative range including the 5th percentile (z5) quantile regression predictor, the 50th percentile (z50) quantile regression predictor and the 95th percentile (z95) quantile regression predictor, as individual deviation z-scores for each brain region, representing the difference from normative GMV calculated across all HC individuals.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Main paper, Methods and materials section, GMV normative deviation calculation and subtypes clustering

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper describes clustering stability assessment using 10-fold cross-validation with 1000 permutations to select the optimal number of clusters based on Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) scores. This suggests some form of internal validation within the discovery dataset. However, it is unclear whether the normative model itself (the quantile regression model trained on HC) was cross-validated or whether this cross-validation only applies to the clustering step.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: We assessed the stability of clustering based on scores of the adjusted rand index (ARI) for 2-5 clusters which were divided by using the hierarchical cutoffs (Hubert & Arabie, 1985). We then chose the clustering solution with the highest averaged ARI following 10-fold cross-validation with 1000 times permutations, as the optimal clustering results.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.location: Main paper, Methods and materials section, GMV normative deviation calculation and subtypes clustering

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not describe using an independent hold-out set from the same domain (i.e., independent HC participants from the same site) to validate the normative model's performance. All 404 HC participants appear to be used to build the normative model, and validation is focused on replicating the GMV deviation patterns in a separate clinical cohort (Dataset 2), not on validating the normative model itself on independent HC data.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: We recruited 114 MDD patients, 60 BD patients and 404 healthy controls (HC). ... In this study, the 174 drugfree patients constitute the discovery dataset (dataset 1), while the 268 medicated patients comprise the validated dataset (dataset 2). We validate the distinct GMV deviations between subtypes in dataset 1 and assess the correlations of regional deviation findings between dataset 1 and dataset 2.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.location: Main paper, Methods and materials section, Participants and GMV normative deviation calculation and subtypes clustering

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study validates GMV deviation-based subtyping findings in a replication cohort (Dataset 2) consisting of 268 medicated patients recruited from the same site. The group-averaged regional GMV deviation values (z50 maps) were found to correlate significantly between Dataset 1 and Dataset 2 in both subtypes (subtype 1: r=0.29, p<0.05; subtype 2: r=0.45, p<0.0001), and the top 10 regions with supra-normal/infra-normal deviations were consistent across datasets. However, this is not a validation of the normative model in a completely different domain (e.g., different scanner, site, or population); rather, it is a replication of the subtyping pattern in a different clinical cohort from the same site and scanner. The replication cohort differs in medication status (medicated vs. drug-naive/drug-free), which may be considered a different 'domain' in a limited sense.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: The group averaged regional GMV deviations values (z50 maps) were mapped and found to show significantly correlations between datasets 1 and 2 in both subtypes 1 (r=0.29, p<0.05) and 2 (r=0.45, p<0.0001) (online Supplementary Fig. S4). The top 10 regions with supra-normal deviations in frontal cortex in subtype 1 and regions with infra-normal deviations in frontal cortex and cingulated cortex in subtype 2 were found consistent in both datasets 1 and 2 (online Supplementary Table S9, Table S10). ... To validate the imaging phenotypes, we involved 268 patients who received medication treatment as the replication cohort. These patients were also recruited and scanned at the First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.location: Main paper, Results section, GMV deviations differences between the two subtypes; Methods and materials section, Participants

clinical_dataset.answer: Discovery cohort: First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University (MDD and BD patients); Validation cohort: First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University (MDD and BD patients, medicated)

clinical_groups_n.answer: Discovery cohort (Dataset 1): MDD:114; BD:60; Validation cohort (Dataset 2): MDD:142; BD:126

clinical_groups_age.answer: Discovery cohort (Dataset 1): MDD: 28.7±11.1 years; BD: 27.8±8.5 years; Validation cohort (Dataset 2): Subtype 1: 29.20±8.89 years; Subtype 2: 28.45±9.47 years

clinical_groups_sex.answer: Discovery cohort (Dataset 1): MDD: F70.2% M29.8%; BD: F61.7% M38.3%; Validation cohort (Dataset 2): Subtype 1: F68% M32%; Subtype 2: F64.2% M35.8%

deviation_metric.answer: Individual deviation z-scores at 5th percentile (z5), 50th percentile (z50), and 95th percentile (z95). Patients categorized as supra-normal (z95 > 1.96), normal, or infra-normal (z5 < -1.96) for each brain region. Average abnormality rate (overall percentage of GMV deviation) and average abnormality extent (mean z95 or z5 values) calculated for each subtype.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests to compare clinical measures (HAMD, HAMA, BPRS total scores) between subtypes with FDR correction (pFDR < 0.05). WCST cognitive performance compared between subtypes and HC using two-sample t-tests with FDR correction. Symptom network analysis using graph theory: Pearson correlations between HAMD items, HAMA items, and BPRS factors (r >= 0.2 threshold); global network density and strength compared between subtypes; paired t-tests for network strength differences. Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression to link GMV deviations to gene expression (transcriptome-imaging associations). Gene enrichment analysis using Metascape (pFDR < 0.05). Virtual histology analysis using permutation tests to assess overlap of PLS genes with cell-type specific genes (pFDR < 0.05). Chi-squared tests to compare overlap of genes with cell types between subtypes. Polygenic risk score (PRS) analysis using logistic regression to test associations of PRS-AD and PRS-MDD with subtypes (pFDR < 0.05), with Nagelkerke's pseudo-R² to quantify variance explained.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Two distinct subtypes were identified: subtype 1 with increased GMV in frontal cortex, cognitive impairment, higher AD genetic risk, and transcriptionally associated with AD pathways and endothelial/oligodendrocyte cells; subtype 2 with globally decreased GMV, more severe depressive symptoms, higher MDD genetic vulnerability, and transcriptionally related to microglia and inhibitory neurons.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Two neuroimaging subtypes of mood disorders were identified using hierarchical clustering based on individual GMV deviations. Subtype 1 (n=112; 74 MDD, 38 BD) showed supra-normal GMV deviations in frontal cortex (orbitofrontal, rostral middle frontal, cingulate, paracentral regions; z95 > 1.96) and infra-normal deviations in temporoparietal regions (z5 < -1.96). This subtype exhibited significantly impaired cognitive function (WCST-PE: t=4.00, pFDR=0.001; WCST-CR: t=-3.65, pFDR=0.001; WCST-CC: t=-3.63, pFDR=0.001; WCST-TE: t=3.61, pFDR=0.001) compared to HC. PRS-AD analysis showed significant associations at four SNP thresholds (p<1.0e-06, p<1.0e-03, p<1.0e-02, p<0.1), explaining 4.2%, 5.9%, 4.1%, and 5.4% of variance in subtype 1, respectively (pFDR < 0.05). PLS1-subtype 1 genes (26.38% covariance explained; r=0.52, p=0.0017) were enriched in Alzheimer's disease pathways, cell/blood morphogenesis, and cellular component processes (pFDR < 0.05), and significantly overlapped with endothelial and oligodendrocyte cell-type genes compared to subtype 2 (chi-squared test, pFDR < 0.05). Subtype 2 (n=62; 40 MDD, 22 BD) showed widespread infra-normal GMV deviations in frontal, temporal, parietal, and cingulate cortex and supra-normal deviation in occipital cortex (z95 > 1.96, z5 < -1.96). This subtype had significantly higher HAMD total scores than subtype 1 (t=2.67, pFDR=0.025), with more prominent guilt (t=2.16, p=0.032), early insomnia (t=2.369, p=0.019), insight (t=2.16, p=0.032), and general somatic symptoms (t=2.219, p=0.028). Symptom network analysis revealed higher global network density (0.51 vs 0.42) and strength (6.76 vs 5.24) in subtype 2 compared to subtype 1, with higher global network strength under the same density threshold (t=10.17, p=1.0e-06). PRS-MDD analysis showed significant association at p<1.0e-03 threshold (NSNPs=1357), explaining 10.8% of variance in subtype 2 (pFDR < 0.05). PLS1-subtype 2 genes (r=0.48, p=0.0039) were enriched in ion transport, calcium signaling, trans-synaptic signaling, and response to stress biological processes (pFDR < 0.05), and significantly enriched in microglia-related genes (117 overlapped genes, permutation pFDR=0.005) and marginally enriched in inhibitory neuron-related genes (157 overlapped genes, permutation pFDR=0.057). The GMV deviation patterns were validated in an independent replication cohort (Dataset 2, n=268 medicated patients): group-averaged regional GMV deviation values correlated significantly between datasets in subtype 1 (r=0.29, p<0.05) and subtype 2 (r=0.45, p<0.0001), with the top 10 regions showing consistent supra-normal/infra-normal deviations across both datasets.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: First, the use of gene expression profiles from healthy human brain (AHBA) to explain GMV deviation changes is limited, as transcription in patients could differ from healthy brains. Additionally, AHBA gene expression data includes right hemisphere data for only two participants, restricting representation of spatial correlation between entire brain transcriptional level and GMV deviations. Second, the genetic data sample size was small (subtype 1: n=19; subtype 2: n=29 for PRS analysis). Third, only WCST scores were used to test cognitive functions between subtypes; other cognitive batteries would be valuable in future work. Fourth, the study did not obtain specific data about illness severity of the first episode in medication-free patients and was unable to detect associations between GMV alterations and prior depressive/anxious/psychotic symptoms.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Authors suggest limited immediate clinical application but future utility may lie in stratifying subgroups and testing associations with other outcomes (functioning, persistence, non-psychotic psychopathology). The findings indicate a potential advancement toward categorical subtyping and development of precise individualized treatment for patients with MDD and BD. The supra-normal dominant subtype with cognitive impairment may represent patients at risk for Alzheimer's disease, while the infra-normal subtype with severe depressive symptoms may benefit from treatments targeting microglia, inhibitory neurons, and GABAergic signaling dysfunction. Refining the present diagnostic system with objective biological measures (e.g., supra-normal and infra-normal GMV) would generate more biologically homogeneous categories, critical for developing more personalized and effective treatments.

general_notes.general_notes: This study is a transdiagnostic approach examining both MDD and BD patients as a combined mood disorder continuum. The discovery cohort consisted of drug-naïve and drug-free patients to minimize medication confounders, while the validation cohort included medicated patients. Both cohorts were recruited from the same site (First Affiliated Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China) and scanned using the same scanner (Signa HDx 3.0T MRI system, GE Healthcare). Patients were diagnosed using DSM-IV-TR criteria via Structured Clinical Interview (for age ≥18 years) or K-SADS-PL (for age <18 years). Clinical assessments included HAMD-17, HAMA-14, BPRS, and WCST. Genetic analyses were performed on a subset of participants (subtype 1: n=19; subtype 2: n=29; HC: n=160) using Illumina Global Screening Array-24 v1.0 BeadChip. Genotype imputation was conducted using GenoImpute with mean sample-level r²=0.736. PRS calculations used GWAS data from Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (AD: 71,880 cases, 383,378 controls from Jansen et al. 2019; MDD: 135,458 cases, 344,901 controls from Wray et al. 2018). Transcriptomic data were from Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA) with 6 donors, 3702 tissue samples, 20,737 genes, 58,692 probes; only left hemisphere data were used (34 regions × 10,027 genes matrix) due to limited right hemisphere data. The study identified two subtypes using Ward's linkage hierarchical clustering on z50 GMV deviation maps, with optimal k=2 clusters selected based on highest averaged ARI scores from 10-fold cross-validation with 1000 permutations. The distribution of MDD vs BD diagnoses did not differ between subtypes (χ²=0.04, p=0.83), supporting transdiagnostic subtyping. Subtype discrimination was not driven by demographic characteristics (no differences in age, gender, or education between subtypes). The study addresses a critical gap in understanding heterogeneity in mood disorders by integrating neuroimaging, transcriptomics, and genetic data across multiple biological scales. This is one of the first studies to link individual-level GMV deviations to cell-type specific transcriptomic profiles and polygenic risk in mood disorders.
